summary: US stocks bounced Monday (S&P +0.7%, Nasdaq +0.8%) as Anthropic's IPO filing revived AI and chip buying, while the dollar firmed, the 10-year held near 5% and Brent eased from six-month highs. Positioning is light ahead of a hawkish-leaning Fed (Thu 05:00 Sydney), MSFT/GOOGL earnings and the BOJ on Friday.
events_next_24h: Wed 11:15 AUD RBA Gov Bullock speaks (medium)
Wed 11:30 AUD Q3 CPI and trimmed mean CPI (high)
Wed 12:00 NZD RBNZ rate decision and statement (high)

NKD.why: Nikkei fell a third day to its lowest close since July 30 on chip selling, but US chips rallied ~3% overnight and the yen weakened, so signals conflict.
NKD.risk: A strong follow-through in Tokyo chip names, or renewed AI selling, would set the direction.

NQ.why: Nasdaq rebounded on the Anthropic IPO filing after two losing weeks, but AI valuation doubts, ~5% yields and MSFT/GOOGL earnings Wednesday keep it two-sided.
NQ.risk: A clean break either way on mega-cap earnings or a hawkish Fed tone.

ES.why: S&P rose 0.7% but remains below its 50-day average after two weekly losses, with the Fed and a third of the index reporting this week.
ES.risk: Fed guidance toward a December hike, or strong hyperscaler earnings.

YM.why: Dow lagged the tech-led bounce (+0.3%); no clear macro edge before the Fed and heavy earnings week.
YM.risk: A decisive Fed message or broad earnings beats.

RTY.why: Small caps rose 0.4% but lagged; near-5% yields and Fed hike talk are a headwind, offset by firm US data like the Dallas Fed beat.
RTY.risk: Yields breaking back above 5% would tilt it bearish.

6J.why: Yen was Monday's weakest major (USD/JPY ~157.5), yet a hawkish BOJ hold with ~75% December hike odds and carry unwinding support it.
6J.risk: BOJ Friday guidance or a hawkish Fed widening the rate gap.

6E.why: EUR/USD slid to ~1.118, extending 17-month lows, on a wide Fed-ECB rate gap and an energy-driven stagflation squeeze on Europe.
6E.risk: A dovish Fed Wednesday or a hawkish ECB surprise Thursday.

6B.why: Cable eased with the firmer dollar, but a fully priced BoE November hike supports sterling ahead of Wednesday's budget.
6B.risk: Budget borrowing surprise or shift in BoE hike pricing.

6A.why: AUD sits near 0.70 on rising RBA hike bets, but Q3 CPI lands Wednesday 11:30 Sydney and could swing November pricing either way.
6A.risk: A hot trimmed-mean CPI turns it bullish; a soft one bearish.

ZN.why: 10-year yields near 4.99% have eased from 5.3% this month, but hike bets and oil-driven inflation keep the Fed hawkish.
ZN.risk: Fed signalling a December hike would push yields higher and notes lower.

GC.why: Gold hovers near $4,000 after sliding to multi-week lows on ~5% yields, a firm dollar and Fed hike bets; Monday's small gain didn't change that.
GC.risk: A dovish Fed or a Middle East escalation driving haven demand.

CL.why: Crude pulled back from six-month highs on Iran mediation talks, but Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, the Iran blockade and Libya outages keep supply risk live.
CL.risk: A US-Iran escalation (bullish) or a mediation breakthrough (bearish).
